q: The work extractable from a non-equilibrium state ρ relative to a thermal bath at temperature T with free Hamiltonian H₀ is bounded by the non-equilibrium free energy:
opts: W ≤ F(ρ) − F(γ) = kT·D(ρ||γ) where γ ∝ e^{-H₀/kT} is the Gibbs state
exp: Non-equilibrium free energy: W ≤ F(ρ)−F(γ) = kT·D(ρ||γ_{thermal}). The extractable work is bounded by kT times the KL divergence from the Gibbs state. This is the quantum/classical second law in resource-theoretic form—KL divergence measures the 'thermodynamic resource'.
